gaps.note: Sudden lighting change implies an edit.

stage_a.note: High energy, upbeat, smiling, and theatrical delivery when breaking the ice block.
Very excited and animated gestures about the product's features and mission.
Friendly, engaging, smiling, and welcoming introduction to the panel.

venture.description: A rugged, solar-powered, rechargeable device that functions as a flashlight, lantern, and cell phone charger.
venture.note: They ask for $150,000 in exchange for 10% of their business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founders introduce the XTorch, a durable solar-powered flashlight, lantern, and charger, demonstrating its toughness by breaking it out of ice.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks how to turn the device on.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene demonstrates the button presses to activate the flashlight and room lantern functions.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori expresses understanding and acts impressed by the light.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene continues the demonstration, showing the table lantern function.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori notes the table lantern function while handling the device.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy adds that it can also be used as a work lantern.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert handles the device and observes its functionality.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene explains the green indicator lights that show the battery charge level.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks how long it takes to fully charge the device using solar power.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene answers that it takes about 22 hours outside to fully charge via solar.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy adds that the device can also be charged using electricity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks how long it takes to charge the device with electricity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy states that it takes only one hour to charge with electricity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy demonstrates how to plug in a USB cable to charge a cellphone.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark makes a vibrating sound joke while holding the device to his face.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene reacts to Mark's joke with amusement.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy jokes that the investors look very scary in the dark.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin shines the flashlight on his face to look intimidating.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark points the light upward, observing its brightness.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert notes that the light would be better if the ceiling were lower.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks for the retail price of the flashlight.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene states the website price is $55.95 and it costs $18.50 to manufacture.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks Gene to repeat the pricing and cost figures.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene repeats the retail and manufacturing costs, noting the next run will cost $14.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan asks Keidy where she is from, noting her Spanish greeting.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy explains she grew up in the Dominican Republic and is familiar with power outages.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks how they came up with the idea for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy recounts living in Equatorial Guinea and getting severely sick with an unknown illness.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene describes doctors saying she was dying, having no power, and using a tiny flashlight to read medication labels.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene concludes the story by stating that Keidy survived the ordeal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy cheerfully confirms that she survived.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert cheers for Keidy's survival.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin acknowledges that the traumatic experience was the motivation for the product.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan remarks that it is a very dramatic reason for inventing a flashlight.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks how their product is different from any other flashlight.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy jokes about not getting Gene started on the flashlight comparison.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene insists it is not a flashlight but a solar-powered rechargeable light and power device.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori challenges Gene, stating that such devices are commonly known as flashlights.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark agrees with Lori, reiterating that it is known as a flashlight.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene pushes back, refusing the term flashlight and emphasizing it is a safety power device.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark jokes that it is the device formerly known as a flashlight.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene contrasts his device with a $10 hardware store flashlight, noting it can't act as a lantern or charger.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark counters that a $55 device might be able to do those things.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert dismisses Mark's point, siding with Gene's feature comparison.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori laughs and says her head still goes to calling it a flashlight.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes about not asking the flashlight community for their opinion.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks what their marketing plan is, noting it's a marketing play.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene states they are currently operating in 38 countries.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks for confirmation that they are already in 38 countries.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene confirms they work with non-profits to help people without light.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if they sell the devices to non-profits or give them away.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy explains they used to sell to non-profits but recently changed their business model.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks directly if they are a charity or a business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy answers that they are both a charity and a business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark clarifies that they went commercial and now want to sell to everyday consumers.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene confirms they want to go direct to consumer online at a lower price point.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks for their sales figures from the previous year.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene states they sold $53,000 worth of product last year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what they project for their sales this year.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene projects $90,000 for the current year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks if that figure is year-to-date or a projection.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene confirms that $90,000 is what they think they will do.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan asks how much they have sold year-to-date.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene states they have done $36,000 year-to-date.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks what their sales were when they started with NGOs in 30 countries.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene answers that it was about $30,000 for the whole year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if there is anything proprietary in their technology.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene explains they analyzed many existing products to design theirs, but doesn't explicitly address proprietary status.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark challenges Gene for talking around the question instead of answering it.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene asks Mark to restate the question.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark repeats the question about whether anything is proprietary.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene points to the lenses and buttons they designed as their proprietary elements.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if those elements are actually proprietary to them.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene says they designed the firmware and the physical parts.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert presses Gene, stating he isn't answering whether it's proprietary or not.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene deflects by asking Robert to explain what he means by proprietary.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark defines proprietary as owning the exclusive rights to it.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks explicitly if they have intellectual property or a patent.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene admits they do not have a patent on the device.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin praises the product but advises a direct-to-consumer model at a lower price, urging them to focus on profit.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene repeats Kevin's catchphrase to make money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy enthusiastically agrees to make money.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark states the product is great but exits because they lack sales and a clear marketing plan.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan exits, stating he likes the product but wouldn't pay the high retail price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy playfully begs the remaining sharks in Spanish for an offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan jokes that Robert needs to give them a good offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert criticizes their awful sales and lack of market understanding, warning they will get crushed.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert offers to buy the entire company for $400,000, stating he doesn't want to be partners.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene immediately counters Robert's offer, asking for one million dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin reacts with surprise to Gene's high counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene justifies the high valuation by citing their connections with non-profits worldwide.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert argues that connections aren't enough without sales, emphasizing why they need him.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert revises his offer, raising it to $500,000 for the entire company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy expresses surprise at the increased offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark remarks that the negotiation just got interesting.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori exits, noting the product is good but faces too much competition to be investable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Keidy thanks Lori for her feedback.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if they are rejecting his offer, pointing out their lack of IP and sales.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene counters Robert's revised offer with $750,000.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin reacts to the new counter-offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark reacts emphatically to Gene's counter.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert refuses the $750,000 counter-offer, stating he won't go that high.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gene asks Robert what he is going to do next.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert officially exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark wishes the founders good luck as they leave.

decisions.note: Great product but you haven't demonstrated sales or a plan to blow it out.
Likes the product but wouldn't pay $60 for it.

decisions.terms: I'll give you $400,000 for 100% of the business.
decisions.note: Not impressed with business acumen, wants to buy the entire company.

decisions.terms: I would go up to $500,000 for 100%.

decisions.note: Tries to meet in the middle.

decisions.terms: No way I'm going up to that.

record.notes: The narrator states at 9:42 that three sharks are out, but Kevin never explicitly exits on screen. The video has a commercial break teaser and recap from 9:24 to 9:50 which is excluded.
